Topics · Meaning and purpose

Why am I on this earth?

Made a successor on earth, to worship a Lord who needs nothing, and given a trust. A purpose for every day.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention, O Muḥammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority."[17] They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and declare Your perfection?"[18] He [Allāh] said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."

Translator's notes

[17] Khalīfah: successor, or generations of man, one following another. [18] An additional meaning is "...and we purify ourselves for You."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:30

Translation

One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”

Original · Hebrew

וְקָרָ֨א זֶ֤ה אֶל־זֶה֙ וְאָמַ֔ר קָד֧וֹשׁ ׀ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מְלֹ֥א כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃

Isaiah · 6:3

World English Bible

If a human being were only an accident, your question would have no answer beyond what you make of it. The verse offers another scene. Before the human exists, the role is announced: a successor on earth. The angels ask: will he spread corruption and shed blood? Yet the reply comes: I know what you do not. The human has a role before earning it, and a whole life to live it.

A question for you

Which seems the truer description of a human being?

If you sayOne who ruins and sheds blood.
ThenThat view has its evidence, and the verse does not deny it. It only says this is not all.
If you sayOne who learns, builds and repairs.
ThenThat is what the verse after it points to (2:31): the names.
If you sayBoth at once.
ThenThat makes the role a choice, not a nature. The trust has its own Step.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ٥٦ مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ٥٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.

Quran · Adh-Dhariyat 51:56-57

Translation

The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·

Acts · 17:24-25

World English Bible

It may seem strange that a person should be made to worship, as if God needed it. The next verse cuts that thought off: I want no provision from them, and no food. Worship adds nothing to Him. If He has no need of it, whatever good is in it is ours. It may be what joins a person to their source, as a root joins a tree to the ground.

A question for you

Who needs worship, according to these verses?

If you sayThe human being.
ThenThen it is a gift before it is a task. What does that mean for your prayer or your silence?
If you sayNo one. I see no need for it.
ThenAn honest position. The question of direction in life remains, and has another Step.
If you sayI am not sure.
ThenThat is fine. The verse denies any need on His side, and you can begin from that.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَـٰٓئِفَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَـٰتٍ لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِى مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌۢ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may try you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:165

Translation

“O God of my ancestors and Lord of mercy, who made all things by your word; and by your wisdom you formed man, that he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by you, and rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and execute judgment in uprightness of soul,

Original · Ancient Greek

Θεὲ πατέρων καὶ Κύριε τοῦ ἐλέους σου, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ πάντα ἐν λόγῳ σου, καὶ τῇ σοφίᾳ σου κατεσκεύασας ἄνθρωπον, ἵνα δεσπόζῃ τῶν ὑπὸ σοῦ γενομένων κτισμάτων, καὶ διέπῃ τὸν κόσμον ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ, καὶ ἐν εὐθύτητι ψυχῆς κρίσιν κρίνῃ·

Wisdom · 9:1-3

World English Bible

If you are a successor, what is in your hands is not yours forever. The verse says people were made successors, some raised above others in rank, to be tried in what they were given. Your mind, money, children and time are less prizes than trusts. This adds a question to every day: what are you doing with what you were given? And the verse closes on forgiveness and mercy for one who falls short.

A question for you

What in your hands feels most like a trust?

If you sayPeople I care for.
ThenThen your stewardship begins at home.
If you sayMy work or my talent.
ThenThere is a Step on what this means in an ordinary job.
If you sayMy time and health.
ThenPerhaps those are what is given most quietly of all.

The same in the other books

If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it.
